title: Adaptive staged-trim admission with stitchable partial outputs and regional failover policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive admission controller that performs staged trimming of requests under pressure, returns stitchable partial outputs when necessary, and integrates region-aware failover rules driven by SLO priorities. Rationale: We need a mechanism that preserves high-priority tenant SLOs while maximizing useful work returned to callers during transient overloads and multi-region failures. Instead of an all-or-nothing reject, the system should progressively trim non-critical parts of the request (context, optional tool calls, lower-priority completion tokens) and return a markerized partial response that clients can stitch or retry against fallback endpoints.
design_summary:
- Admission stages: accept-full, accept-trimmed (drop non-essential tokens/tools), accept-partial (stop generation early and return stitch token), reject.
- Decision inputs: tenant SLO weight, request deadline, recent tail-latency percentiles (p95/p99), per-region capacity credit, historical fidelity delta for this prompt template.
- Stitchable partial output: standardized envelope that includes last-complete-token, KV-checkpoint id, model-variant used, and a recommended follow-up (retry at lower fidelity or go to regional fallback).
- Regional failover: requests hitting capacity thresholds will be routed to next region if the tenant policy allows cross-region fallback; otherwise use partial output path.
- Circuit breaker interplay: integrate with existing CB to escalate from accept-trimmed to reject when error+latency signals cross thresholds.
- Telemetry: new spans + tags for admission_stage, trimmed_fields, stitch_token, region_route, and SLO-credit consumption.
- Backwards compatibility: clients that don't understand stitchable outputs get a concise human-readable partial message and an HTTP header X-Redwood-Partial: true.
acceptance_criteria: SLO preservation: under synthetic overload, top-tier tenants maintain p95 latency within 1.2x baseline and error-rate < 0.5% increase.
End-to-end tests: deterministic unit tests for admission decision matrix and integration tests covering staged trim -> stitchable output -> client stitch flow.
Canary rollout: feature toggled, 2% traffic in us-west-2 for 72 hours with automatic rollback on SLO regression.
Observability: dashboard with admission_stage distribution, trimmed_token counts, stitchable-output rate, regional failover counts, and per-tenant SLO burn rate.
mitigation_plan: If rollout shows unexpected SLO regressions: 1) Immediately disable accept-partial in the canary flag; 2) Increase capacity margin for the affected region by shifting reserved pools; 3) Revert to reject-only policy for tenants with adverse impact while we analyze trimmed field correlations.
implementation_notes:
- Add admission_stage to request context early in pipeline so downstream runtime can apply trimmed execution paths.
- Create a lightweight 'stitch token' format (base64 JSON blob, signed) referencing model checkpoint + KV-cache snapshot id.
- Trimming rules are pluggable per-route: e.g., conversational requests -> trim older turns first; embeddings -> trim optional metadata; reranking -> reduce candidate set before model inference.
- New config: tenant.shedding.profile with weights for fidelity vs latency, and tenant.allow_cross_region_failover boolean.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for decision matrix permutations.
2) Load test harness that injects p99 latency spikes and verifies admission stages transition as expected.
3) Chaos test: simulate region egress loss and observe automatic partial-output and failover behavior.
4) Client-side example app in SDK repo demonstrating stitch logic.
rollout_plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime-1.22.staged_trim flag.
- Phase 1: Internal traffic only, smoke tests.
- Phase 2: Canary customers with opt-in, 2% traffic for 72h.
- Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% with monitoring and manual gates.
- Phase 4: Default on for new tenants, opt-in controls for legacy ones.
risk_assessment: Medium. New response format requires careful client compatibility handling; risk of under-trimming resulting in missed SLO targets if heuristics are tuned too conservatively. Rollback path is straightforward via flags and tenant-level policies.
